advances: Conditional bounds for an actual midpoint and actual mixed slabs of attaining caps. The envelope gap remains in the distinct-cost bound.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The own-depth root concavity of 4e868f774de77608 applies to the actual fibers of the convex body and gives $\Delta\ge0$. It also gives $F(Y_m)>0$ since the endpoints are interior to positive fibers. By 1ec728c26c11b368 there is an attaining nonvertical closed cap through $Y_m$. In any such cap the endpoint margins are opposite because $L$ is affine. If $s_e=L(Y_e)\ge0$, the parallel cap $\{L\ge s_e\}$ contains $Y_e$ and is a subset of $H$. Their exact difference in original mixed mass is $T_e$, because their set difference is $\{0\le L<s_e\}$. Therefore $D(Y_m)\ge D_e+T_e$. If $s_e>0$, the nonzero continuous normal and a ball around $Y_e$ in its own fiber give a positive-volume portion with $0<L<s_e$, so $T_e>0$.

At a common $\theta$, average the equal endpoint objective values and compare with the midpoint value. The affine term cancels, giving $D(Y_m)\le (D_0+D_1)/2-\lambda\Delta$. Equality of endpoint objectives gives the formula for $A$. If $A>0$, the upper bound is strictly below $D_0$, so an attaining cap cannot contain $Y_0$ even on its boundary. The opposite margins then give $s_1>0$, and the shift estimate gives $T+\lambda\Delta\le A/2$. For $A=0$, every containing halfspace at the midpoint contains at least one endpoint, so its mass is at least $D_0$. This forces equality in the depth upper bound and $\Delta=0$ because $\lambda>0$. A positive margin would force the critical cap mass above $D_0$ by the shift estimate. The opposite margins are therefore both zero.

For two parameter values, the vector exchange from pk-w36-coarse-vector-envelope-work puts $A$ between $\theta_0\cdot\delta w$ and $\theta_1\cdot\delta w$. On the joining segment write $\ell_i(t)=D_i+[\theta_0+t(\theta_1-\theta_0)]\cdot w(Y_i)$. Their difference $\ell_1(t)-\ell_0(t)$ equals $B_0(t-t_*)$. The envelope is convex on this segment as a maximum of affine functions and equals $\ell_0(0)$ at zero and $\ell_1(1)$ at one. Subtracting $\ell_0(t_*)$ from the chord joining those endpoint values gives $t_*(1-t_*)B_0$. This bounds $B$ from above, and $B\ge0$ since both lines are available. At the crossing the common value equals the average of the endpoint objectives at $\theta_*$. The affine $p$ terms again cancel when comparing to the midpoint. This gives $D(Y_m)\le (D_0+D_1)/2+B-\lambda_*\Delta$. Combining with $D(Y_m)\ge D_e+T_e$ proves the signed budget and its absolute-value bound.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body, $n,d\ge1$, with positive summed $d$-volume $\mu$ on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Let $D(Y)$ be its raw closed-halfspace depth and $F(Y)$ the $d$th root of raw ordinary depth in the actual fiber of $Y=(z,x)$, using zero on null fibers. Fix either $p(Y)=z$ or $p(Y)=Y$. Put $w(Y)=(F(Y),p(Y))$ and $E(\theta)=\max_{Y\in S}[D(Y)+\theta\cdot w(Y)]$ for $\theta=(\lambda,b)$ with $\lambda\ge0$. Suppose $Y_0,Y_1$ are two selected sources in the interiors of their positive fibers and their midpoint $Y_m$ belongs to $S$. Write $D_i=D(Y_i)$, $F_i=F(Y_i)$ and $\Delta=F(Y_m)-(F_0+F_1)/2\ge0$.

If both are active at the same $\theta=(\lambda,b)$ with $\lambda>0$, label $D_0\ge D_1$ and put $A=D_0-D_1$. Then $D(Y_m)\le(D_0+D_1)/2-\lambda\Delta$ and $A=\lambda(F_1-F_0)+b\cdot[p(Y_1)-p(Y_0)]$. If $A>0$, every nonvertical attaining closed cap $H=\{L\ge0\}$ through $Y_m$ excludes $Y_0$ and strictly contains $Y_1$. Its slab $T=\mu\{0\le L<L(Y_1)\}$ is positive and satisfies $T+\lambda\Delta\le A/2$. If $A=0$, then $D(Y_m)=D_0$, $\Delta=0$, and both endpoints lie on each such critical plane.

If $Y_i$ is active at $\theta_i$, let $A=D_0-D_1$, $\delta w=w(Y_1)-w(Y_0)$ and suppose $B_0=(\theta_1-\theta_0)\cdot\delta w>0$. Put $t_*=(A-\theta_0\cdot\delta w)/B_0\in[0,1]$ and $\theta_*=\theta_0+t_*(\theta_1-\theta_0)$. At this parameter the endpoint objective lines meet. The gap $B$ between the envelope and their common value satisfies $0\le B\le t_*(1-t_*)B_0\le B_0/4$. For any nonvertical attaining cap through $Y_m$ containing endpoint $Y_e$, where $e\in\{0,1\}$, let $T_e=\mu\{0\le L<L(Y_e)\}$. Then
$$
T_e+\lambda_*\Delta\le\frac{D_{1-e}-D_e}{2}+B\le\frac{|A|}{2}+B,
$$
where $\lambda_*$ is the first coordinate of $\theta_*$.
title: Actual midpoint slab charges for affine depth costs
